findings.title: canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission now unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking standard OAuth2 token exchange
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo() (and exchangeToPermission()) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() was not overridden, so calls to AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...) fell back to the legacy, functional ClientPermissions implementation even when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 was enabled. Now that MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, any call to canExchangeTo (used by the standard OAuth2 token-exchange grant to check the per-client 'token-exchange' permission) will throw an unchecked RuntimeException instead of evaluating/denying the request. Because AdminPermissions.management(...) dispatches to V2 purely based on the global Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 flag (not a per-realm setting), enabling this preview feature on a server breaks token exchange for every client in every realm on that server, not just realms that opted into the new permission schema.

findings.title: Client/role/group removal cleanup can crash with UnsupportedOperationException when V2 evaluator is selected
findings.body: The ProviderEventListener registered here calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) (and similarly for roles/groups) when a RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent occurs. The whole block is now gated by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (line 77), but the inner call to management() independently decides between V1 and V2 based on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. If both the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and the new ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature flags are enabled at the same time (nothing in this code prevents that, and both are server-wide flags), management() will return MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled() (and similarly users()/groups() for the respective events) now throws UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally (see ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled). This exception would propagate out of the event listener during a client/role/group deletion, breaking that admin operation.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot return real client IDs and can return the bogus literal 'Clients'
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() to the result for any matching resource with the given scope granted. However, per-client resources created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (server-spi-private .../AdminPermissionsSchema.java, around line 104) are never given a 'type' attribute (only resource.updateScopes(...) is called, there is no resource.setType(resourceType)), so findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) will never match them - individual per-client granted permissions are silently excluded from the result. Conversely, the catch-all 'all clients' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() does have its type explicitly set to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and its name is literally the string 'Clients'. If an all-clients permission for the requested scope exists, that resource matches findByType and the literal string 'Clients' gets added to the returned Set<String> as if it were an actual client ID. Any caller treating the result as a set of real client identifiers will get incorrect/garbage data.

findings.title: getResourceName() was not updated to handle the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE (returning 'All users' for the catch-all resource and the username for individual user resources) but has no corresponding branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE even though this PR adds Clients as a fully supported resource type. For permissions targeting Clients, this method falls through to 'return resource.getDisplayName();', which, for resources created via getOrCreateResource/resourceStore.create (no display name set), returns the raw resource name - the client's internal UUID rather than a friendly label like 'All clients' or the client's clientId. This produces a poor/incorrect UX anywhere this name is surfaced (e.g. admin console or REST responses listing permissions for the Clients resource type).

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the 'all-clients' resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), if the per-client resource is not found, the code falls back to resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether getResourceTypeResource returned null. If the 'Clients' catch-all resource does not exist for the resource server (e.g. schema not initialized for that resource server, or data inconsistency), resource will be null and findByResource(server, null) is likely to throw an NPE (and if it somehow doesn't, resource.getScopes() later in the method would).

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Clients resource-type permission CRUD/resource lifecycle and getClientsWithPermission
findings.body: UserResourceTypePermissionTest provides dedicated coverage for permission/resource representation semantics for the Users resource type (testCreateResourceTypePermission, testCreateResourceObjectPermission, testFindByResourceObject, testDelete - verifying orphan resource cleanup, and testUpdate). PermissionClientTest, added by this PR for the new Clients resource type, only contains behavioral tests (manage/configure/view/mapRoles scenarios) and has no equivalent tests verifying that creating/removing scope permissions for Clients correctly creates/cleans up the underlying Resource records, nor any test exercising ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(). Given the identified bug in getClientsWithPermission (not finding real per-client resources, and potentially returning the literal 'Clients'), this gap means the regression would not be caught by the test suite.
